items.title: Finite orthogonal sums of self-adjoint operators and of bounded operators
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), the choice
hypothesis of the cited definitions of the adjoint. Fix an integer $r\ge1$, let
$H_{1},\dots,H_{r}$ be complex Hilbert spaces with inner products linear in the
first argument ([[def-hilbert-space]]), and let
$$H:=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H_{l},\qquad \bigl\langle (x_{l}),(y_{l})\bigr\rangle:=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle x_{l},y_{l}\rangle_{H_{l}},$$
be their orthogonal sum. For each $l$ let $A_{l}:D(A_{l})\subset H_{l}\to H_{l}$
be a densely defined self-adjoint operator
([[def-adjoint-of-a-densely-defined-unbounded-operator]],
[[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]]) and put
$$D(A):=\Bigl\{(x_{l})\in H:\ x_{l}\in D(A_{l})\ \text{for all }l,\ \sum_{l=1}^{r}\|A_{l}x_{l}\|_{H_{l}}^{2}<\infty\Bigr\},\qquad A(x_{l}):=(A_{l}x_{l}).$$
Then:

(a) $H$ is a complex Hilbert space, $D(A)$ is a dense linear subspace of $H$,
and $A:D(A)\to H$ is a linear operator;

(b) $A$ is symmetric and self-adjoint, and
$\|Ax\|^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|A_{l}x_{l}\|_{H_{l}}^{2}$ for every $x\in D(A)$;

(c) if $B_{l}\in\mathcal B(H_{l})$ for every $l$
([[def-bounded-linear-operator]]), then $B:=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}B_{l}$, defined
by $B(x_{l}):=(B_{l}x_{l})$ for all $(x_{l})\in H$, is bounded with
$$\|B\|=\max_{1\le l\le r}\|B_{l}\|$$
([[def-operator-norm]]), its adjoint is
$B^{*}=\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}B_{l}^{*}$ ([[def-hilbert-space-adjoint]]), and $B$
is unitary if every $B_{l}$ is unitary.

No assertion is made about infinite orthogonal sums: only the finite case is
proved here.

items.title: Unitary identifications of the component-valued wave-function space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix integers
$d\ge1$ and $r\ge1$, let $H:=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with the Euclidean
integral pairing ([[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]],
[[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]],
[[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]), let
$$H^{(r)}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr),\qquad \langle f,g\rangle:=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}(x)\overline{g_{l}(x)}\,dx,$$
and let $\mathbb C^{r}$ carry the standard inner product with orthonormal basis
$e_{1},\dots,e_{r}$ ([[def-hilbert-space]],
[[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]).
Write $H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}$ for the completed tensor product of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]] with inclusion $\kappa$.
Then:

(a) the map
$$\Psi_{0}\Bigl((f_{l})\Bigr):=\bigl(x\mapsto(f_{1}(x),\dots,f_{r}(x))\bigr)$$
is a well-defined unitary isomorphism $\bigoplus_{l=1}^{r}H\to H^{(r)}$, and
$$\|\Psi_{0}(f)\|_{H^{(r)}}^{2}=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\|f_{l}\|_{H}^{2},\qquad \langle\Psi_{0}(f),\Psi_{0}(g)\rangle=\sum_{l=1}^{r}\langle f_{l},g_{l}\rangle_{H};$$

(b) the assignment on elementary tensors
$\Theta_{0}(\kappa(u\otimes e_{l})):=\iota_{l}(u)$, where $\iota_{l}(u)$ is
the $r$-tuple with $u$ in slot $l$ and $0$ elsewhere, extends uniquely to a
surjective linear isometry $\Theta:H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}\to H^{(r)}$
(so $\Theta$ is unitary), and
$\Theta(\kappa(u\otimes z))=\sum_{l=1}^{r}z_{l}\,\iota_{l}(u)$ for all
$u\in H$, $z=\sum_{l}z_{l}e_{l}\in\mathbb C^{r}$;

(c) for every $a\in L^{\infty}(\mathbb R^{d})$ and every $v\in\mathbb R^{d}$ one
has the intertwining identities
$$\Theta^{-1}\bigl(a\cdot\Theta(w)\bigr)=(M_{a}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w,\qquad \Theta^{-1}\bigl(T_{v}^{(r)}\Theta(w)\bigr)=(T_{v}\otimes I_{\mathbb C^{r}})w\qquad(w\in H\widehat{\otimes}\mathbb C^{r}),$$
where $M_{a}$ is multiplication by $a$, $T_{v}$ is the Euclidean translation
$T_{v}h:=h(\cdot-v)$ of [[lem-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-momentum-operators-self-adjoint]]
clause (c), $T_{v}^{(r)}$ is its componentwise action on $H^{(r)}$, and the
bounded amplifications are those of [[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]].

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 1.4, printed pages 45-47 (PDF pages 57-59): orthogonal sums and tensor products of Hilbert spaces

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 6.1 printed pages 105-110 (PDF pages 113-118): composite systems, product states and amplitudes of a composite system; Section 7.4 printed pages 158-161 (PDF pages 166-169): finite-dimensional spin states as an internal factor of the state space

items.title: Componentwise position and momentum operators on the component-valued wave-function space
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the choice hypotheses of the
cited scalar operator and spectral suppliers. Fix integers $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$. Let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the
component-valued space of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]
with its componentwise inner product, let $Q_{j}^{(1)},P_{k}^{(1)}$ be the
scalar position and momentum operators on $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]], and let
$\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary Plancherel transform with
$\widehat f(\xi)=\int f(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on $L^{1}$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Write
$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}\mathcal F_{2}\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$
for its componentwise version, with $\Psi_{0}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] clause (a).
Define, componentwise,
$$D(Q_{j}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (Q_{j}f)_{l}:=x_{j}f_{l},$$
$$D(P_{k}):=\bigl\{f=(f_{l})\in H^{(r)}:\ D_{k}f_{l}\text{ exists in }L^{2}\ \text{for all }l\bigr\},\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
where $D_{k}$ is the weak derivative of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]].
Write $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the classes whose components
lie in $W^{m,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]),
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ for the componentwise Schwartz
class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]). Then:

(a) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are the orthogonal sums
$\bigoplus_{l}Q_{j}^{(1)}$ and $\bigoplus_{l}P_{k}^{(1)}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]; in particular
$Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are densely defined and self-adjoint with the displayed
domains;

(b) $\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}$ is unitary,
$$D(P_{k})=\bigl\{f\in H^{(r)}:\ \xi_{k}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})\bigr\},$$
and for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
$$\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}(P_{k}f)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{k}\,\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)}f(\xi)\qquad\text{for almost every }\xi;$$

(c) the componentwise translation $T_{a}^{(r)}f:=f(\cdot-a)$, $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$,
is unitary, leaves $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$
invariant, satisfies $D_{k}(T_{a}^{(r)}f)=T_{a}^{(r)}(D_{k}f)$ for
$f\in W^{1,2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$$T_{a}^{(r)}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}Q_{j}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k}),\quad T_{a}^{(r)}P_{k}\bigl(T_{a}^{(r)}\bigr)^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(d) for every $f\in D(P_{j})$,
$$\lim_{t\to0}\frac1t\bigl(T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}f-f\bigr)=-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}f \qquad\text{in }H^{(r)},$$
so the strongly continuous one-parameter unitary group
$t\mapsto T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}$ has generator $-\frac{i}{\hbar}P_{j}$ and
$$T_{te_{j}}^{(r)}=\exp\Bigl(-\frac{i}{\hbar}tP_{j}\Bigr)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R),$$
the exponential being the spectral-calculus flow of the self-adjoint operator
$P_{j}$.

items.title: Canonical commutation relations on the component-valued core and commutation with the internal factor
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix integers $d\ge1$,
$r\ge1$ and $\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with
the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let
$\mathcal S^{(r)}:=\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ be the componentwise
Schwartz class ([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]]), and let $\Psi_{0}$
and $\Theta$ be the unitaries of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]]. For
$S=(S_{lm})\in M_{r}(\mathbb C)$ write
$$S_{\times}f:=\Bigl(\sum_{m=1}^{r}S_{lm}f_{m}\Bigr)_{l}\qquad(f\in H^{(r)}).$$
Then:

(a) $\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all $j,k$,
$Q_{j}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$ and
$P_{k}\mathcal S^{(r)}\subseteq\mathcal S^{(r)}$, and on $\mathcal S^{(r)}$ the
canonical commutation relations hold:
$$(Q_{j}P_{k}-P_{k}Q_{j})f=i\hbar\,\delta_{jk}f\qquad(f\in\mathcal S^{(r)});$$

(b) $S_{\times}$ is bounded with $\|S_{\times}\|=\|S\|_{\mathrm{op}}$
([[def-operator-norm]]), and
$$S_{\times}D(Q_{j})\subseteq D(Q_{j}),\quad Q_{j}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}Q_{j}f\ (f\in D(Q_{j})),\qquad S_{\times}D(P_{k})\subseteq D(P_{k}),\quad P_{k}S_{\times}f=S_{\times}P_{k}f\ (f\in D(P_{k}));$$

(c) the spectral projection-valued measures of $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}},\qquad E_{P_{k}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)*}M_{\mathbf 1_{\{2\pi\hbar\xi_{k}\in B\}}}\mathcal F_{2}^{(r)} \qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
where $M_{g}$ is multiplication by $g$; consequently
$S_{\times}E_{Q_{j}}(B)=E_{Q_{j}}(B)S_{\times}$ and
$S_{\times}E_{P_{k}}(B)=E_{P_{k}}(B)S_{\times}$ for every Borel $B$, and for
unitary $V\in U(r)$ and every $f\in H^{(r)}$
$$\bigl\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)V_{\times}f\bigr\|=\bigl\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)f\bigr\|,\qquad \bigl\|E_{P_{k}}(B)V_{\times}f\bigr\|=\bigl\|E_{P_{k}}(B)f\bigr\|;$$

(d) under the tensor identification $\Theta$ the operator $S_{\times}$
corresponds to the bounded amplification $I\otimes S$ of
[[lem-nrqm-composites-bounded-tensor-maps]], that is
$\Theta^{-1}S_{\times}\Theta=I\otimes S$; in particular the internal-factor
operators commute with the spatial ones in the sense of (b).

references.title: G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 2.1, printed pages 55-58 (PDF pages 67-70): position, momentum and the canonical commutation relation; Section 8.1, printed pages 173-175 (PDF pages 185-187): algebraic position and momentum methods

J. Binney and D. Skinner, The Physics of Quantum Mechanics, Section 2.3, printed pages 24-28 (PDF pages 32-36): the commutator [x,p]=i hbar in the position representation and its role in the operator calculus

items.title: The momentum representation of the componentwise kinematics
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$, $r\ge1$ and
$\hbar>0$, let $H^{(r)}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ with the
componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]], let $U$ be the
unitary of [[lem-nrqm-composites-momentum-fourier-jacobian]] clause (c), which
on Schwartz classes acts by
$$(U\psi)(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi(x)\,dx,$$
and put $U^{(r)}:=\Psi_{0}\bigl(\bigoplus_{l}U\bigr)\Psi_{0}^{-1}$ with
$\Psi_{0}$ as in [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]].
Then:

(a) $U^{(r)}:L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dx;\mathbb C^{r})\to L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$
is unitary; for $f=(f_{l})\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$,
$$(U^{(r)}f)_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-d/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}f_{l}(x)\,dx \qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
$U^{(r)}f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
$\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|U^{(r)}f(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp
=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx$;

(b) $U^{(r)}D(P_{k})=D(M_{p_{k}})$, where $M_{p_{k}}g(p):=p_{k}g(p)$ on
$D(M_{p_{k}})=\{g\in L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r}):p_{k}g\in L^{2}\}$, and
$$U^{(r)}P_{k}=M_{p_{k}}U^{(r)};$$
equivalently $(U^{(r)}P_{k}f)(p)=p_{k}(U^{(r)}f)(p)$ for every $f\in D(P_{k})$
and almost every $p$;

(c) for every $f\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C^{r})$ and every $j$,
$$U^{(r)}(Q_{j}f)(p)=i\hbar\,\frac{\partial}{\partial p_{j}}\bigl(U^{(r)}f\bigr)(p) \qquad(p\in\mathbb R^{d}),$$
and both sides are Schwartz classes; no identity of unbounded operators on the
full domain of $Q_{j}$ is asserted;

(d) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{d}$, with $T_{a}^{(r)}$ the componentwise
translation of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]
clause (c),
$$U^{(r)}T_{a}^{(r)}U^{(r)-1}=M_{e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}},$$
the bounded multiplication operator by the unimodular function
$p\mapsto e^{-ia\cdot p/\hbar}$;

(e) under $\Psi_{0}$ the operator $U^{(r)}$ is the orthogonal sum
$\bigoplus_{l}U$; no physical identification of $U^{(r)}f$ with a measured
momentum distribution is made by this lemma.

G. Teschl, Mathematical Methods in Quantum Mechanics, 1st edition 2009, Section 7.1, printed pages 161-167 (PDF pages 173-179): the Fourier transform, its unitary extension and the momentum representation

items.title: The massive spin-s particle model of the framework: state space, operators, units and frame readings
items.statement:
**(a) Adopted model and state space.** Adopt the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 for a declared particle of mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\tfrac32,\dots\}$ and internal factor
assigned as in the identical-particle and spin postulate P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]). Put $r:=2s+1$ and take
as the model's one-particle state space the complex Hilbert space
$$H_{s}:=L^{2}\bigl(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}\bigr) =\Bigl\{f:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb C^{r}\ \text{measurable}:\ \int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\|f(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx<\infty\Bigr\}\Big/\!\sim,$$
the quotient by equality almost everywhere, with inner product
$\langle f,g\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}\sum_{l=1}^{r}f_{l}\overline{g_{l}}\,dx$
linear in the first argument ([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]).
Thus an element of $H_{s}$ is a class of functions, not a function, and
pointwise values of a state are not defined; the position density is read from
the class through the observables of clause (b) and the observable and
probability postulate P2 ([[post-nrqm-framework-state-and-composition]],
[[def-nrqm-state-geometry-framework-state-space]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Its dimension
in the conventions of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)1
is $\ell^{-3/2}$ per component. P5 presents the same space as the completed
tensor product $L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)\widehat\otimes\mathbb C^{r}$
with the spin factor carrying the representation of P6; the unitary
identification of the two descriptions and the componentwise reading of
componentwise operators are those of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-component-valued-wavefunction-identifications]] and
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]. The orthonormal
basis $(e_{m})_{m=-s,\dots,s}$ of $\mathbb C^{r}$ is the basis fixed by P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii)).

**(b) Position and momentum.** The model's $j$-th position and $k$-th momentum
are the componentwise operators $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a): for
$f=(f_{l})$, restricted to the classes with $x_{j}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ respectively
with $D_{k}f_{l}\in L^{2}$ for all $l$,
$$(Q_{j}f)_{l}(x):=x_{j}f_{l}(x),\qquad (P_{k}f)_{l}:=-i\hbar\,D_{k}f_{l},$$
with $D_{k}$ the weak derivative and $\hbar$ the action constant of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. These are the scalar operators of
[[def-nrqm-magnetic-and-detection-position-and-momentum-operators]] applied
componentwise. The model assigns to $(Q_{j},\mathrm m)$ and to
$(P_{k},\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})$ the status of assigned sharp observables in
the sense of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]
clause (a), with the units of [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4; both are densely defined and self-adjoint by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (a). On the
Schwartz core they satisfy the componentwise canonical commutation relations,
and they commute with the internal-factor operators of clause (c) in the sense
of [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clauses (a),(c).

**(c) Internal factor.** For $i\in\{1,2,3\}$ let $S_{i}=\hbar J_{i}$ be the
self-adjoint endomorphisms of $\mathbb C^{r}$ of the spin assignment P6
([[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]] clause (ii),
[[prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices]]), and let the model read
them on $H_{s}$ as the matrix actions
$$(S_{i}f)_{l}:=\hbar\sum_{m=1}^{r}(J_{i})_{lm}f_{m}\qquad(l=1,\dots,r),$$
that is, as the amplifications $I\otimes S_{i}$ under the tensor
identification of clause (a) ([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]]
clause (d)). Their declared unit is the unit of action ([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]
clause (d)4). The factor is internal bookkeeping: it is not a spatial
coordinate, not a rotating body and not a relativistic spinor, and the model
assigns no position or worldline to it.

**(d) Momentum-space representative.** With $U^{(s)}$ the unitary of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] for $r=2s+1$, the
**momentum-space representative** of a preparation vector $\psi\in H_{s}$ is
$\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3},dp;\mathbb C^{r})$; for a
Schwartz class $\psi$ it is the componentwise Fourier transform
$$(\psi_{p})_{l}(p)=(2\pi\hbar)^{-3/2}\int_{\mathbb R^{3}}e^{-ip\cdot x/\hbar}\psi_{l}(x)\,dx,$$
and its dimension is $(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}})^{-3/2}$ per component
([[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] clause (d)2). By
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] clause (b), $P_{k}$ acts on the
momentum representative by multiplication by $p_{k}$; this is the model's
momentum reading and no measured momentum distribution is identified with
$|\psi_{p}|^{2}$ by this definition.

**(e) Frame reading.** The model's inertial frames are the global coordinate
charts of P5; frame changes are the Galilean transformations of P5, with
parameters and units as in [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]. This
definition uses P5's frame class only. The transformation law of state
representatives under a change of inertial frame is a derived statement about
the model's operators and is established by the covariance theorems of this
page for translations and boosts; it is not an additional assumption of this
definition, and no Lorentz transformation law is claimed.

**(f) Status.** Clauses (a)-(e) record the readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6 in the
terminology of this page and fix the objects used by its theorems. They assert
no time evolution beyond what the autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 assigns
([[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]
clause (iv)), no preparation or apparatus model, no detection model and no
empirical result. Massless particles, relativistic matter, radiation, singular
or unbounded potentials and boundary or confined realizations are separate
model assumptions with their own domains and self-adjointness statements; none
is obtained from this definition.

items.physical_scope: The kinematic reading of the massive-particle model postulate P5 for one particle of spin label s and mass parameter m>0: the component-valued state space L^2(R^3;C^(2s+1)) with its class reading and internal factor, the componentwise position and momentum operators with their declared units, the internal spin operators as matrix actions, the momentum-space representative, and the frame reading of the model. The item fixes terminology and readings of P1, P2, P5 and P6; it asserts no dynamics beyond what P4 assigns, no apparatus or detection model, no empirical identification of any species, and excludes massless, relativistic, singular-potential, boundary and radiation models, which require their own assumptions.

items.title: Position and momentum outcome laws of the massive spin-s model
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(b) there is a unique regular projection-valued measure $G$ on the Borel sets
of $\mathbb R^{3}$ with
$$G(B_{1}\times B_{2}\times B_{3})=E_{Q_{1}}(B_{1})E_{Q_{2}}(B_{2})E_{Q_{3}}(B_{3})$$
for all Borel $B_{1},B_{2},B_{3}$, namely $G(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{B}}$, and its
scalar law is the model's Born position law,
$$\mu^{G}_{\psi}(B)=\|G(B)\psi\|^{2}=\int_{B}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(d) for every unitary $V\in U(r)$, with $V_{\times}$ the matrix action of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] clause (b),
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi},\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{V_{\times}\psi}=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi};$$

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$, so an exact value is an idealization outside
the sharp finite-resolution reading.

items.title: Translation covariance of the massive spin-s kinematics and of its bounded-potential dynamics
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and internal-factor postulate P6 read
through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a particle
of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ and translations
$T_{a}:=T_{a}^{(r)}$ ($r=2s+1$) of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] clause (c), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, and let $V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$
be real, bounded and measurable with $V_{a}(x):=V(x-a)$; write
$$H_{V}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k=1}^{3}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V},\qquad D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r}),$$
for the model's free-plus-bounded-potential energy operator
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (c) applied componentwise, assembled by
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-orthogonal-sums-of-self-adjoint-operators]]), with flow
$U_{V}(t)=\exp(-itH_{V}/\hbar)$ in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]] clause (b). Then:

(a) for every $a\in\mathbb R^{3}$ the operator $T_{a}$ is unitary,
$T_{a}D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$, $T_{a}D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$, and
$$T_{a}Q_{j}T_{a}^{-1}=Q_{j}-a_{j}I,\qquad T_{a}P_{k}T_{a}^{-1}=P_{k};$$

(b) **Outcome-law covariance.** For every unit $\psi\in H_{s}$ and Borel
$B\subseteq\mathbb R$,
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-a_{j}),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{T_{a}\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B):$$
translating the preparation by $a$ translates the position law by $a$ and
leaves every momentum law unchanged;

(c) **Dynamics covariance.** With $H_{V}$ and $H_{V_{a}}$ the energy operators
of the potentials $V$ and $V_{a}$,
$$T_{a}H_{V}T_{a}^{-1}=H_{V_{a}},\qquad T_{a}U_{V}(t)T_{a}^{-1}=U_{V_{a}}(t)\qquad(t\in\mathbb R);$$
in particular, if $V$ is invariant under translation by $a$ (equivalently
constant almost everywhere when this holds for every $a$), then $T_{a}$ leaves
$H_{V}$ and its flow invariant, and the free flow ($V=0$) commutes with every
translation;

(d) **Frame reading.** The model reads the inertial-frame change
$t'=t$, $x'=x+a$ of P5 (a change of spatial origin; the parameter $a$ has the
unit of length, [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]) on state
representatives by $\psi'(x')=\psi(x'-a)=(T_{a}\psi)(x')$; this is the
translation convention of the model, consistent with P5's frame class, and
clauses (b) and (c) are its covariance consequences for the outcome laws and
for the bounded-potential dynamics;

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and it concerns the componentwise massive model with real bounded
measurable potentials only; singular or unbounded potentials, confined or
boundary realizations, massless and relativistic models and radiation are
separate model assumptions for which no translation covariance is asserted.
No apparatus, laboratory identification or empirical result is recorded.

The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics, holds for real bounded measurable potentials only, and asserts nothing about singular or unbounded potentials, boundary realizations, relativistic models, radiation, apparatuses or empirical results.

items.title: Galilean boost covariance of the free massive spin-s model and the moving-frame reading
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the
autonomous-dynamics postulate P4 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]], and the kinematics and
massive-particle model postulate P5 and internal-factor postulate P6 read
through [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a particle
of mass parameter $m>0$ and spin label $s$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's
state space with componentwise operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$
([[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]]), let
$\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law of an assigned sharp
observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$, let
$H_{0}:=\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}$ with domain
$D(H_{0})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and flow
$U_{0}(t)=\exp(-itH_{0}/\hbar)$, and for real bounded measurable
$V:\mathbb R^{3}\to\mathbb R$ let $H_{V}$ and $U_{V}$ be the operator and flow of
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]], with
$D(H_{V})=W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ and
$V_{u}(x,t):=V(x-ut)$. For $u\in\mathbb R^{3}$ and $t\in\mathbb R$ define the
**boost operator** $B_{u}(t)$ componentwise by
$$\bigl(B_{u}(t)\psi\bigr)(x):=\exp\Bigl(\frac{i}{\hbar}\Bigl(m\,u\cdot x -\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}t\Bigr)\Bigr)\psi(x-ut).$$
Then:

(a) for every $u,t$ the operator $B_{u}(t)$ is unitary,
$B_{u}(t)^{-1}=B_{u}(t)^{*}$, and it maps $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
and $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ onto themselves;

(b) $B_{u}(t)D(Q_{j})=D(Q_{j})$ and $B_{u}(t)D(P_{k})=D(P_{k})$; for
$f\in D(Q_{j})$ and $g\in D(P_{k})$, respectively,
$$Q_{j}B_{u}(t)f=B_{u}(t)(Q_{j}+u_{j}tI)f,\qquad P_{k}B_{u}(t)g=B_{u}(t)(P_{k}+mu_{k}I)g.$$
For a Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$ and
$a\in\mathbb R$, write $B-a:=\{b-a:b\in B\}$. Consequently, for every
unit $\psi$ and Borel $B\subseteq\mathbb R$
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B-u_{j}t),\qquad \mu^{P_{k}}_{B_{u}(t)\psi}(B)=\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B-mu_{k});$$

(c) **free covariance.** $B_{u}(t)U_{0}(t-s)=U_{0}(t-s)B_{u}(s)$ for all
$s,t\in\mathbb R$; in particular the freely evolved boosted preparation equals
the boost at time $t$ of the initial boosted preparation,
$$B_{u}(t)U_{0}(t)\psi=U_{0}(t)B_{u}(0)\psi\qquad(\psi\in H_{s});$$
and the conjugated free Hamiltonian identity
$$B_{u}(t)^{-1}H_{0}B_{u}(t)=H_{0}+u\cdot P+\frac{m|u|^{2}}{2}I$$
holds on $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$ (in the chart velocity
$v=-u$ of clause (e) it reads $H_{0}-v\cdot P+\frac{m|v|^{2}}{2}I$), the
operator form of the frame change on the free generator;

(d) **moving-frame bounded-potential model.** For every real bounded
measurable $V$ and every $u$, the two-parameter family
$$W_{u}(t,s):=B_{u}(t)\,U_{V}(t-s)\,B_{u}(s)^{-1}$$
consists of unitaries preserving $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$, and
for every $s\in\mathbb R$ and $\psi_{0}\in W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{r})$
the curve $t\mapsto W_{u}(t,s)\psi_{0}$ takes values in $W^{2,2}$, is
differentiable as an $L^{2}$-valued curve and satisfies
$$i\hbar\frac{d}{dt}\psi(t)=\Bigl(\frac{1}{2m}\sum_{k}P_{k}^{2}+M_{V_{u}(\cdot,t)}\Bigr)\psi(t),\qquad \psi(s)=\psi_{0};$$
it is unique among maps $w:\mathbb R\to W^{2,2}$ that are differentiable
into $L^{2}$ and satisfy this equation in $L^{2}$ for every $t$ with
$w(s)=\psi_{0}$;

(e) **Frame reading and scope.** The model reads the inertial-frame change
$t'=t$, $x'=x+ut$ of P5 (the new chart moves with velocity $-u$ relative to the
old one) on state representatives by $\psi'(x',t)=(B_{u}(t)\psi(\cdot,t))(x')$;
clauses (b)-(d) are the covariance consequences of that reading for the laws
of the free model and for the bounded-potential dynamics in the moving frame.
The statement is conditional on P2, P4, P5 and P6 and the cited mathematics,
concerns the componentwise massive model with real bounded measurable
potentials only, and asserts no Lorentz covariance, no photon limit, no
covariance for singular or unbounded potentials and no worldline of an
unmeasured particle; no apparatus or empirical result is recorded.

items.title: Scope and empirical status of the massive-particle kinematics items
items.statement:
## What the pair establishes

The items of this pair are conditional consequences of the framework's
postulates and of the cited mathematics. [[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]]
founds the spin-$s$ model on the state space $H_{s}=L^{2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C^{2s+1})$
with the componentwise position and momentum operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-componentwise-position-and-momentum]] proves that these
operators are self-adjoint with their maximal domains and provides the Fourier
representation and the translation identities;
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] proves the
canonical commutation relations on the Schwartz core, identifies the spectral
measures and proves that the internal factor commutes with the spatial
measures; [[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]] constructs the
momentum representation;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] derives the position and momentum
outcome laws of the spin-$s$ model, including the Born density
$\|\psi(x)\|^{2}_{\mathbb C^{2s+1}}$ and the momentum density
$\|\psi_{p}(p)\|^{2}$;
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-translation-covariance]] and
[[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-boost-covariance]] establish the covariance of these
laws and of the bounded-potential dynamics under the Galilean translations and
boosts of the model's frame class. All of this is conditional on P1, P2, P4,
P5 and P6 and on the cited mathematical suppliers; none of it is a statement
that any physical system is exactly described by the model.

## Empirical status of the parameters

The mass parameter $m>0$ and the spin label $s$ are model parameters: within
the framework they are declared values, and the identical-particle and spin
postulate assigns to a species its mass, spin, statistics and couplings as
empirical model parameters with uncertainty. This pair derives no value of
$m$ or $s$, records no measurement and asserts no species identification; the
units in which $m$, $\hbar$, $Q_{j}$ and $P_{k}$ are read are those of
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]], and the exact defining constants
of the current SI recorded there are unit conventions, not measurements of
this framework.

## What is not claimed

The outcome laws are sharp-law statements: an exact position or momentum value
has probability zero in every preparation, finite-resolution outcomes are
Borel bins, and no detector, efficiency, resolution or sampling model is
introduced. The covariance theorems hold for the free model and for real
bounded measurable potentials; they assert nothing for singular or unbounded
potentials, confined or boundary realizations, massless particles, radiation
or relativistic matter. The internal factor is bookkeeping: it is not
identified with a spatial rotation, a classical angular momentum or a
relativistic spinor, and no empirical consequence of the spin assignment alone
is derived. The identification of the operators $Q_{j},P_{k}$ with concrete
laboratory procedures remains a tested identification under the preparation
and apparatus postulate, external to this pair.

items.title: The Gaussian position and momentum packet of the massive model
items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 and the massive-particle model
postulate P5 read through
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] for a spinless particle
($s=0$, $r=1$) of mass parameter $m>0$, and assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Fix a width
$\sigma>0$ and define
$$\psi_{\sigma}(x):=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})},\qquad x\in\mathbb R^{3}.$$
Then:

(i) $\psi_{\sigma}\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$ with
$\|\psi_{\sigma}\|=1$, so its ray is a pure preparation of the model and
$\psi_{\sigma}\in D(Q_{j})\cap D(P_{k})$ for all $j,k$, with
$D_{j}\psi_{\sigma}=-\sigma^{-2}x_{j}\psi_{\sigma}$;

(ii) with $U$ the momentum transform of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-momentum-representation]], $U\psi_{\sigma}=\psi_{\sigma_{p}}$
where $\sigma_{p}:=\hbar/\sigma$, that is
$$(U\psi_{\sigma})(p)=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|p|^{2}/(2\sigma_{p}^{2})};$$

(iii) the position law of $Q_{j}$ in the preparation $[\psi_{\sigma}]$ has
density $(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-t^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$ in the coordinate
$t=x_{j}$, hence mean $0$ and variance $\sigma^{2}/2$; the momentum law of
$P_{k}$ has density $(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-1/2}e^{-p^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$ in
the coordinate $p=p_{k}$, mean $0$ and variance
$\sigma_{p}^{2}/2=\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$; the product of the two standard
deviations is $\hbar/2$;

(iv) the joint position law of the three position observables has density
$|\psi_{\sigma}(x)|^{2}=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|x|^{2}/\sigma^{2}}$, and
the momentum representative has density
$|(U\psi_{\sigma})(p)|^{2}=(\pi\sigma_{p}^{2})^{-3/2}e^{-|p|^{2}/\sigma_{p}^{2}}$
against $dp$.

The example is an exact model computation in one family of preparations; no
dynamics, detection model or empirical value is involved, and the variance
statements are properties of this family only.

The item uses the model's own sharp outcome laws; it computes no dynamics, models no measurement, asserts no uncertainty theorem for arbitrary preparations and records no empirical result.

items.title: The plane wave as a generalized momentum eigenfunctional
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Fix $d\ge1$,
$\hbar>0$ and $k\in\mathbb R^{d}$, and define on the Schwartz space
$\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ of
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]] the conjugate-linear functional
$$u_{k}(\varphi):=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}e^{ik\cdot x}\,\overline{\varphi(x)}\,dx.$$
Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the negative-sign $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform,
$\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)=\int\psi(x)e^{-2\pi ix\cdot\xi}dx$ on
$L^{1}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$
([[def-fourier-transform-on-l-one-of-rn]], [[thm-plancherel]]). Then:

(a) $u_{k}$ is well defined, conjugate-linear and continuous in the Schwartz
topology. Writing $p_{\alpha,0}(\varphi)=\sup_x|x^{\alpha}\varphi(x)|$ for the
seminorms of [[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]], one has the explicit
bound
$$|u_{k}(\varphi)|\le\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}|\varphi(x)|\,dx\le C_{d}\sum_{\alpha\in\{0,2\}^{d}}p_{\alpha,0}(\varphi),\qquad C_{d}:=\left(\int_{\mathbb R}(1+t^{2})^{-1}\,dt\right)^{d}<\infty;$$
moreover $u_{k}(\varphi)=\mathcal F_{2}\bigl(\overline{\varphi}\bigr)\bigl(-\tfrac{k}{2\pi}\bigr)$
for every $\varphi$;

(b) for every $\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ and every
$j\in\{1,\dots,d\}$, with $P_{j}\varphi:=-i\hbar\,\partial_{j}\varphi$ the
componentwise momentum action on Schwartz classes,
$$u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}\,u_{k}(\varphi),\qquad u_{k}(P_{j}^{2}\varphi)=(\hbar k_{j})^{2}\,u_{k}(\varphi):$$
the functional is a generalized eigenfunctional of every momentum component
with eigenvalue $\hbar k_{j}$;

(c) there is no $L^{2}$ class $F\in L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$ with
$u_{k}(\varphi)=\int_{\mathbb R^{d}}F(x)\overline{\varphi(x)}\,dx$ for all
$\varphi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$; in particular the functions
$x\mapsto e^{ik\cdot x}$ and its nonzero scalar multiples are not elements of
$L^{2}(\mathbb R^{d};\mathbb C)$;

(d) the statements are purely mathematical: $u_{k}$ is a conjugate-linear
functional on the Schwartz space, no normalizable class represents it, and no
physical state, preparation or outcome probability is attached to it by this
example.

$$AB-BA=i\hbar I .$$

items.statement:
Adopt the observable and probability postulate P2 in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] and the
kinematics and massive-particle model postulate P5
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]]), and
assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Consider the following
hypothetical confined-model extension of the kinematics: a spinless particle
of mass $m>0$ is restricted to an interval $(0,L)$ of length $0<L<\infty$ in
one spatial direction, with Hilbert space $L^{2}(0,L;\mathbb C)$, and the
model declares its momentum to be the formal differential expression
$$T:=-i\hbar D,\qquad D(T):=\bigl\{u\in H^{1}(0,L;\mathbb C):\ u^{*}(0)=u^{*}(L)=0\bigr\},$$
with $H^{1}$ and the continuous trace $u^{*}$ as in
[[def-nrqm-intervals-hilbert-sobolev-spaces]]. Then, in that hypothetical
model:

(a) $T$ is densely defined and symmetric, but not self-adjoint; its adjoint is
$$T^{*}=-i\hbar D,\qquad D(T^{*})=H^{1}(0,L;\mathbb C),$$
without boundary condition;

(b) no self-adjoint extension $S\supseteq T$ has domain contained in the
Dirichlet class $D(T)$: there is no self-adjoint realization of the formal
momentum on $(0,L)$ that keeps the Dirichlet condition on its domain;

(c) for every self-adjoint extension $S\supseteq T$ and every $n\ge1$, the
normalized Dirichlet function $u_{n}(x)=\sqrt{2/L}\,\sin(n\pi x/L)$ lies in
$D(S)$ but is not an eigenvector of $S$; consequently a momentum
quantization read off from the Dirichlet eigenfunctions is not a statement
about any self-adjoint realization of the interval momentum;

(d) therefore $T$ is not an assigned sharp observable of the model in the
sense of P2, and no outcome law of a momentum observable of the confined
model exists until the model declares a self-adjoint realization of its
momentum. An explicit family of self-adjoint extensions of $T$ is
$\hbar P_{\theta}$, $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$, where $P_{\theta}=-iD$ is the
self-adjoint operator of
[[thm-nrqm-intervals-twisted-periodic-momentum-domain]]; the scaled operator
$\hbar P_{\theta}$ acts as $-i\hbar D$ on the domain
$\{u\in H^{1}(0,L):u^{*}(L)=e^{i\theta}u^{*}(0)\}$ and has units of momentum.
These domains impose a twisted-periodic condition rather than Dirichlet
conditions; nothing here claims that any member of that family, or any other
realization, describes a laboratory apparatus.

items.physical_scope: A conditional warning about a hypothetical confined-model extension of the massive-particle kinematics: if a model confines a spinless particle to an interval and declares the formal momentum -i hbar d/dx on the Dirichlet domain, then that operator is symmetric but not self-adjoint and hence is not an assigned sharp observable of the observable and probability postulate; no self-adjoint extension keeps the Dirichlet domain, and the Dirichlet eigenfunctions are not momentum eigenfunctions of any such extension. The item asserts no experiment, no apparatus realization and no claim that confinement models are physically realized; it excludes any assertion about which self-adjoint realization, if any, describes a laboratory device.

items.title: What the worked items of the companion page establish
items.statement:
## Three worked items

**The Gaussian packet.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-gaussian-position-momentum-packet]]
computes, in the spin-zero massive model, the normalized Gaussian
$\psi_{\sigma}(x)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$, shows
that its momentum representative is again a normalized Gaussian with width
$\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$, and evaluates the position and momentum outcome
densities of the model together with their variances $\sigma^{2}/2$ and
$\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$ and the product $\hbar/2$. This verifies the model's
sharp laws of [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] on a family of
Schwartz preparations; it computes no dynamics, no measurement and no general
uncertainty statement.

**The plane wave as a generalized functional.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-plane-wave-generalized-eigenfunction]]
defines the conjugate-linear functional $u_{k}(\varphi)=\int e^{ik\cdot
x}\overline{\varphi}$ on Schwartz classes, proves the eigenrelation
$u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}u_{k}(\varphi)$, and proves that no $L^{2}$
class represents $u_{k}$. This is the precise sense in which the plane wave is
a generalized momentum eigenfunction: it diagonalizes the momentum action on
the test space while carrying no state or probability density. The framework's
state assignment excludes it as a preparation, in agreement with the model's
atomless sharp laws.

**The boundary warning.** [[texp-nrqm-kinematics-dirichlet-momentum-warning]]
shows, in a hypothetical confined-model extension, that the formal interval
momentum $-i\hbar D$ on the Dirichlet domain is symmetric but not self-adjoint,
that no self-adjoint extension keeps the Dirichlet domain, and that the
Dirichlet functions are not momentum eigenfunctions of any self-adjoint
extension. The companion counterexample
[[cex-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-cannot-hold-for-bounded-operators]] shows that the
canonical commutation relation cannot hold as an identity of bounded
operators at all, so the core relation of
[[lem-nrqm-kinematics-ccr-and-internal-factor-commutation]] is genuinely a
relation on a dense core of unbounded operators rather than a bounded
operator identity.

## What the page does not establish

None of the items is an experiment: no counts, calibration, resolution,
efficiency, background, uncertainty or data comparison appears anywhere on the
page, and no value of $m$, $\hbar$ or any model parameter is measured. The
Gaussian computation is a single family of preparations; the plane-wave item
is a distributional statement without a state; the boundary warning and the
bounded-commutator counterexample are conditional mathematical statements
about hypothetical or bounded models, not claims about apparatuses. In
particular, no item asserts that confined models, twisted-periodic momenta or
any self-adjoint realization describe a laboratory device, and no item draws
conclusions about decoherence, measurement disturbance or relativistic
effects, which belong to other model pages.
